edges.description: Flagellated bacilli are sensed by epithelial TLR5 when they contact the airway surface.
Bacterial contact permits the type III secretion apparatus to inject Exo-family cytotoxic effectors into host cells.
Alveolar macrophages sense the type III secretion apparatus and activate an NLRC4 inflammasome response.
Flagellin sensing induces epithelial inflammatory mediators that converge with T3SS and inflammasome signals to recruit neutrophils.
The type III secretion apparatus can be sensed by macrophages and activate an NLRC4 inflammasome response.
T3SS-competent organisms directly worsen epithelial cytotoxicity, alveolar permeability, bacterial clearance, and mortality in acute lung injury.
Inflammasome-driven IL-1 beta release amplifies cytokine production, phagocytic failure, and pulmonary inflammatory damage.
Alginate-mediated antiphagocytic biofilm growth promotes persistence after mucoid conversion in structurally abnormal airways.
Persistent infection repeatedly exposes the airway to Pseudomonas ligands, cytotoxins, and neutrophilic inflammatory injury.
Alveolar-capillary barrier failure and protein-rich edema impair gas exchange, producing dyspnea.
Diffuse neutrophilic alveolar injury and permeability edema can progress to acute respiratory distress syndrome physiology.
Severe lower-respiratory injury with invasive infection can disseminate or drive a systemic inflammatory response, causing sepsis.
Ventilation and airway instrumentation bypass upper-airway defenses and permit P. aeruginosa to seed the tracheobronchial tree and alveolar compartment.
